items.title: 6.2.7 Length of the Tangent from a Point to a Circle

source_refs.note: Book p. 180-181: 6.2.7 Theorem 3 (length of tangent) with Proof and Figure 6.9

blocks.text:
Theorem 3: The length of the tangent drawn from a point \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) to the circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\) is
\[\sqrt{x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} + c}\]

blocks.alt: On a pale yellow panel, a cyan circle with centre C(-g, -f) and an outside point P(x1, y1); the two magenta tangents from P touch the circle (the upper one at T), CT and CP are magenta, with a right-angle mark and 90 degrees at T.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.9: Tangent PT from P(x1, y1) to the circle with centre C(-g, -f); CT is perpendicular to PT (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.9)

blocks.title: Teaching note
Teaching note
blocks.text:
Our illustration (not from the book): from \(P(4, -1)\) to \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x + 4y = 0\) (the circle of Example 14):
\[|PT| = \sqrt{16 + 1 - 8 - 4} = \sqrt{5}\]
Check with Example 14: the point of contact \((3, -3)\) is at distance \(\sqrt{(4 - 3)^{2} + (-1 + 3)^{2}} = \sqrt{5}\) from \(P\), and so is \((2, 0)\): \(\sqrt{4 + 1} = \sqrt{5}\).

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Length of tangent from \((x_{1}, y_{1})\): \(\sqrt{x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} + c}\).
2. It comes from Pythagoras in the right triangle \(PTC\): \(|PT|^{2} = |PC|^{2} - r^{2}\).
3. The two tangents from one point are equal in length.
4. The coefficients of \(x^{2}\) and \(y^{2}\) must be 1 (see 6.2.8).

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Adding \(r^{2}\) instead of subtracting: \(|PT|^{2} = |PC|^{2} - r^{2}\), the hypotenuse is \(CP\).
2. Using the formula when the equation is, say, \(5x^{2} + 5y^{2} + \ldots = 0\) without dividing by 5 first; the answer would be \(\sqrt{5}\) times too large.
3. Getting a negative number under the root and not noticing that the point is inside the circle.
